item.title: Electron launches for 100th time
item.description: Rocket Lab’s Electron launched for the 100th time on a Nov. 14 mission for a Japanese customer, reaching that milestone faster than any other commercial rocket.

item.title: Starship launches on 15th test, calls off booster catch
item.description: SpaceX launched its Starship vehicle on the company’s first attempt to recover both stages of the rocket but was forced to call off recovery of the Super Heavy booster.

item.title: Axiom Space completes key review for lunar spacesuit
item.description: Axiom Space has completed the critical design review for a spacesuit it is developing for NASA’s Artemis missions as it also works on a simplified version for initial landings.

item.title: Hawkeye 360 to expand commercial business in 2027
item.description: WASHINGTON — Signals intelligence firm Hawkeye 360 plans to expand its commercial offerings in the coming year as part of a broader push to diversify its customer base to include more private sector and international clients, CEO John Serafini told investors during a Nov. 12 earnings call.

item.title: China’s Tianwen-4 Jupiter mission to attempt Callisto moon landing
item.description: HELSINKI — China’s space agency has issued a call for payloads for its Jupiter exploration project, revealing the inclusion of a lander targeting Galilean moon Callisto.

item.title: Blue Origin bows out of NASA commercial space station competition

item.title: Connectivity and control: why militaries relying on Starlink need end-use agreements
item.description: A military that relies on a foreign company for its satellite communications gives up a great degree of control over its own operations. Ukraine, which has relied on Starlink for battlefield communications since the early days of its war with Russia, learned once again in October about the dangers of depending on a foreign capability.
